arguments.comment: Resident loader: current load address ($90 low, $91 page), from X/Y at $F295 and advanced a page per block ($F258).
Resident loader: end address ($92 low, $93 high) = load address + file length from the table at $F2F9; returned in X/Y.
Resident loader: first byte of the file's table entry ($F2F9+4*A), passed with $95 to the drive routines; probably track and sector (not checked).
Resident loader: second byte of the file's table entry ($F2FA+4*A), adjusted at $F2E4; read with $94.

RESIDENT LOADER, load entry (JMP $F236). Call with A = file number ($00-$30, file_table $F2F9) and X/Y = load address (lo/hi). Returns carry clear and X/Y = the end address (one past the last byte), or carry set on a drive error. The title calls it three times: $4166 (file $01, the packed picture, to $A000; the end it returns bounds the unpacker), $420C (file $02, the 4-bit samples, to $1000) and $4079 (file $03, the shop, to $0880). Uses zero page $90-$95 and $E0-$FB
Second loader entry (JMP $F26A): write a file's sectors to disk, same A and X/Y as load_file. Nothing in this snapshot calls it

load_file proper: load_setup (also sends the disk ID), then per sector: end pointer to $F1/$F2 (set_end_ptr), destination page to $EF/$F0 (set_dest_ptr), read_sector_cmd with track $94 and sector $95, wait_transfer for the 256 bytes, next_sector; the page $91 goes up by one each time until $90/$91 reaches the end $92/$93. Only the bytes before the end are stored (the drive still sends whole sectors)
save_file proper: the same sector walk as load_file_body, but each sector goes out through write_sector ($F43A) from the pages at X/Y. No caller in this snapshot

Set up a file transfer: $90/$91 = X/Y (start), $92/$93 = start + length from file_table, $94 = start track, $95 = start sector (made physical by logical_to_physical when the track's interleave is 11). Then sends drive command $0B with $45 $41 (set_disk_id_cmd), which tells the drive to expect disk ID "EA"; a disk with another ID fails its reads

Advance $94/$95 to the next sector of a file: sector = (sector + track_interleave[track]) mod sectors_per_track[track]; when that comes back to 0 every sector of the track has been used and the walk moves to the next track at sector 0, stepping over track 18 (the directory track)
A = file_table start index; returns A = index*11 mod the sector count of track Y, the physical sector that is the index-th in the interleave-11 sequence (0, 11, 1, 12, ... on a 21-sector track)

Resident loader file table, 4 bytes per file, files $00-$30 (49 entries): +0 start track, +1 start sector as an index into that track's interleave sequence (converted to a physical sector at $F2E4), +2/+3 length in bytes (lo/hi). Files $00-$1A are on side 1, $1B-$30 on side 2 (both start again at track 3). Read by load_setup ($F295). Checked: files $0B, $0C, $0E, $0F, $11 and $12 read from side1.g64 with this table equal the snapshot, apart from the bytes of $0B the game writes at run time
file_table +1 column: start sector index of each file (the auto symbol of the indexed read at $F2B4)
file_table +2 column: file length low byte, added to the load address X to make the end pointer $92 ($F29C)

file_table rows from +3 of file $00 to file $0F: length high byte added to Y for $93 ($F2A3). Rows the title uses: file $00 (track 3, $11FF bytes) is the title itself, loaded by the boot to $4000; $01 (track 4, $117F bytes) the packed title picture; $02 (track 5, $20F0 bytes) the samples; $03 (track 6, $1E80 bytes) the shop. File $0B (track 12) is the resident event manager loaded at $F730 by a later stage; file $0C (track 18 sector 18, 3 bytes) is the disk-side ID

file_table rows for files $10-$1F: $10 (track 17, $17D9 bytes), $11 (track 19, $1284 bytes), $12 (track 20, $402C bytes); $13-$1A are other side-1 files; $1B (side 2, track 3, $3780 bytes) is the file event 3 (DOWNHILL) loads. The title loads none of them
file_table rows for files $20-$2F, all on side 2 ($28, track 14, $378D bytes, is the file event 4 (JAM) loads)
file_table row for file $30 (side 2, track 25 index 14, $09A2 bytes), the last entry; the sectors-per-track table follows
Sectors per track, indexed by track 0-35 (entry 0 unused): 21 for tracks 1-17, 19 for 18-24, 18 for 25-30, 17 for 31-35. Read by next_sector ($F2CE) and logical_to_physical ($F2ED)

Sector step per track, indexed by track 0-35: 1 on tracks 1-3, 18 and 35, 11 on all others. next_sector adds it modulo the track's sector count; load_setup multiplies the start index by 11 when it is 11 or more ($F2B2)

Loader transfer state: 0 = idle or finished, $80 = failed (set with carry at $F648), any other value = a sector transfer is pending (set at $F54A to the destination page high nibble, or $10; only zero, negative and positive are ever tested). Written $F4C2/$F54A/$F4AB/$F650, read by wait_transfer ($F553) and bg_receive ($F57E)
Bytes per call for bg_receive ($F57E) plus one: $14, copied to the countdown $F9 there. Read only at $F58A
Status byte returned by drive command $0C, stored by drive_query_status ($F4A5); nothing in this snapshot reads it
Three bytes ($C0 $F3 $CF) that nothing in this snapshot reads by name; reachable only by an out-of-range track index into track_interleave
Store X/Y as the receive pointer $EF/$F0 (absolute addressing of zero page) for the next transfer
Store X/Y as the end pointer $F1/$F2: receive_bytes stops storing when $EF/$F0 reaches it
Send command $80 (bit 7 set): the drive code takes any such command as JMP ($FFFC), a reset of the drive back to its own DOS. No caller in this snapshot

Ask the drive for one sector: command 1 with track Y and sector X, raw mode ($E8=1: every byte stored, no link bytes followed), clears the byte count $F7 and the end flag $E0. Through send_drive_command

Write one sector: command 5 (on the drive, resets its buffer index), 128 commands 3 each carrying two bytes read from ($EF/$F0), then command 4 with track Y and sector X (patched into $F47C/$F477), which writes the drive's buffer to disk, then wait for the drive's one-byte reply. No caller in this snapshot
Operand of an LDA # in write_sector: the sector for the final command 4, patched from X at $F43A
Operand of the second LDA #: the track for command 4, patched from Y at $F43D
Send command $0B with track byte Y and sector byte X; the drive code stores them as the expected disk ID (drive zero page $12/$13). load_setup sends $45 $41, "EA"
Send command $0C and receive the one byte it answers (the drive's last job status) into drive_status_byte $F407. No caller in this snapshot
Mark a reply pending (xfer_state = $10) and fall into wait_transfer
Operand of the LDX # at $F4B2: send_drive_command's caller X, patched at $F4B7 and handed back on both exits ($10 in the title's snapshot: the sector of the last read)
Operand of the LDY # at $F4B4: the caller's Y, patched at $F4BA ($06 in the title's snapshot: track 6, the last read's track)

Send the 3-byte command in $E5 (command), $E6 (track byte), $E7 (sector byte) to the drive code on the serial bus, keeping X/Y (saved into $F4B3/$F4B5, returned by the exit at $F4B2, entered at $F4B1 with carry set on failure). It raises CIA 2 port A bit 3 ($DD00), fails with carry set if bit 7 is already high or bit 6 does not go low then high within 255 polls, drops bit 3, then clocks out 24 bits most significant first: each bit on $DD00 bit 4, strobed by pulsing bit 5. For commands below 3 it marks a reply pending in xfer_state ($F54A). Returns carry clear when the command was taken
wait_transfer's saved Y (written $F55B, restored $F579)
wait_transfer's saved X (written $F55E, restored $F576)

Wait until a pending reply has been received: if xfer_state is non-zero and positive, call receive_bytes until it is 0 (done) or $80 (failed, carry set). Sets the busy flag $F8 so that bg_receive does not run meanwhile; keeps X/Y ($F551/$F552)

Background receive: if no wait_transfer is running ($F8 = 0) and a reply is pending, take up to 19 bytes (count from bg_slice_bytes) and return, so a load can be spread over interrupts. No caller in this snapshot

Receive reply bytes from the drive while the countdown $F9 lasts: for each byte wait (up to $30 polls, else return) for $DD00 bit 7 to go high, then take 8 bits, each read as bit 6 of $DD00 inverted and acknowledged by a pulse on bit 5; bit 7 falling mid-byte means failure (xfer_state = $80). For command 3 and up the single byte is the whole reply. For a sector, raw mode stores each byte at ($EF/$F0) until the end pointer (end flag $E0); the other mode (not used by load_file) takes bytes 0/1 as the next track/sector link and asks for that sector itself ($F63F). After 256 bytes the transfer is done
Loop back to receive_bytes for the next byte of the sector (reached from $F62B while the in-sector count $E1 has not wrapped)

TITLE ENTRY ($4000, file $00, jumped to by the boot). Blanks the screen (VIC $D011 bit 4 off), banks $01 = $25 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O in), then: load_title_picture (file $01, unpacked into the bitmap at $A000), show_title_picture (bitmap mode on, bank 2), load_samples (file $02 to $1000, the picture on screen meanwhile), install_title_irq (raster interrupt at line $FB, which plays the music and animates the colours), music_init. It then waits at $4022 for fire on either joystick port ($DC00 bit 4 for port 2, $DC01 bit 4 for port 1; SPACE also pulls $DC01 bit 4 with the KERNAL's row 7 selected, simulated). On fire: music_stop and one more music_play call to silence the voices, the colour RAM and the screen are put back from the pristine copies at $8400 and $8800, wait_raster_wrap, the raster interrupt is turned off, file $03 (the shop) is loaded to $0880, $FDFF is cleared (the shop's 'event manager not installed' test reads it: $0F6E/$0F83 in file $03 compare it with $55), and the NMI vector is pointed at $0880 and CIA 2 timer A restarted ($DD0E = 1): the next timer underflow raises an NMI that enters the shop, while the CPU spins at $4090. The title never returns
Wait for fire: either port's bit 4 low (port 1 through $DC01, port 2 through $DC00)
Fire pressed: music_stop ($4B17 = $C0), then music_play once to act on it
Copy the pristine colour data $8400 back to colour RAM $D800 (1000 bytes)
Copy the pristine screen $8800 back to $8000 (undo the colour animation)
Load file $03 (the shop program) at $0880
$FDFF = 0: read by the shop at $0F6E/$0F83 (file $03), which loads the event manager while it is not $55
NMI vector = $0880, the shop's entry
Restart CIA 2 timer A (latch left by the last sample); its NMIs are still enabled from $50FC

Spin here until CIA 2 timer A underflows: the NMI (vector $0880 from $4081) leaves the title for the shop's entry, which resets the stack ($0880 LDX #$FF / TXS in file $03), so the NMI never returns here

Per-frame work of the raster interrupt (from title_irq): music_play, then the frame counter $11/$12 goes up and drives four colour animations. (1) 'ELECTRONIC ARTS' on row 0, columns 12-26: screen nibbles $60 from strip_screen and colour RAM from strip_colours, white or yellow, swapping every 32 frames (bit 5 of $11). (2) The three credit lines (rows 19-21, columns 3-16): one colour per row from names_colours, the phase ($11 >> 3) & 3 shifting every 8 frames, so white, light grey and grey roll down the names. (3) The EA logo (rows 19-21, columns 32-39): each column gets ea_sweep_colours[phase + column], the phase ($11 >> 1) & 7 stepping every 2 frames, a highlight sweeping across. (4) The 'SKATE OR DIE!' logo: phase ($11 >> 4) & 7 (16 frames a step, 128 frames a cycle) calls logo_word_on with 0, 1, 2 in phases 0-2, nothing in 3, logo_word_off with 0, 1, 2 in phases 4-6, nothing in 7; the call is skipped on the one frame in 16 where $11 & 15 = 0
Top strip: 15 cells $800C-$801A and their colour RAM
Credit lines: colour RAM rows 19, 20, 21 from column 3 ($DAFB, $DB23, $DB4B), 14 cells
EA logo: colour RAM rows 19-21 from column 32 ($DB18, $DB40, $DB68), 8 columns
Logo word phase: skipped when $11 & 15 = 0

Turn CIA 1's interrupts off ($DC0D = $7F, acknowledged by reading it), wait_raster_wrap, then set the raster compare to line $FB ($D012 = $FB, $D011 bit 7 clear), the IRQ vector $FFFE/$FFFF to title_irq ($414C) and enable the raster interrupt ($D01A = 1). The KERNAL is banked out, so the hardware vector is used directly

Wait until the raster line's low byte ($D012) goes down from one read to the next: each change is compared with the value before it and the loop ends only when the new value is lower, which happens at line 256 (the low byte returns to 0) or at the start of a frame

Raster interrupt handler (line $FB, vector set by install_title_irq): save A, X, Y, acknowledge the VIC ($D019 read and written back), run title_frame (music and colour animation), restore and RTI. CIA 2's sample NMIs can interrupt it

Load file $01 (the run-length packed title picture, $117F bytes) at $A000; its end (X/Y returned by load_file) goes to $0B/$0C as the unpacker's limit. rle_unpack expands it to $1000-$370F: 8000 bytes of multicolour bitmap, 1000 bytes of colour-RAM nibbles, 1000 bytes of screen colours. copy_block then moves the bitmap $1000-$2F3F to $A000 (over the packed file, already consumed), the colour data $2F40-$3327 to $8400 and the screen data $3328-$370F to $8000, and copies $8000 to $8800 as a pristine screen that logo_word_off and the exit restore from. Checked in the simulator: the bytes it leaves at $8400, $8800 and $A000-$BF3F equal the title snapshot's

Black border and background ($D020/$D021 = 0); copy the colour nibbles $8400 to colour RAM $D800 (1000 bytes); VIC bank 2 ($DD00 bits 0-1 = %01: $8000-$BFFF), $D018 = $08 (screen matrix $8000, bitmap $A000), $D016 = $18 (multicolour, 40 columns), $D011 = $3B (bitmap mode, display on, 25 rows)
Load file $02 ($20F0 bytes) at $1000-$30EF: the seven 4-bit guitar samples the music plays through the NMI ($5106). It overwrites the start of the unpacked picture, which has been copied out by then

Copy 256 * Y + X bytes from the pointer $07/$08 to the pointer $09/$0A, one at a time through read_src and write_dst. $0F counts the bytes and $10 the passes; a non-zero X adds a pass, so the first pass copies X bytes and each later one 256. Both pointers are left one past the end, which load_title_picture uses to chain its copies
A = the byte at ($07/$08), then advance $07/$08 (Y = 0 on return)
Store A at ($09/$0A), then advance $09/$0A (Y = 0 on return)

Recolour one word of the 'SKATE OR DIE!' logo, A = 0 (SKATE), 1 (OR) or 2 (DIE!): the word's entry in logo_word_blocks (five bytes at $455E + 5A: screen address lo/hi, width - 1, height - 1, offset) gives a rectangle of cells; the screen nibbles come from logo_word_screen + offset and the colour-RAM nibbles from logo_word_colour + offset, row by row, into the screen at $8000 and colour RAM at screen + $5800 ($D800 + the same cell). The new nibbles swap the logo's white face and brown shadow

Undo logo_word_on for word A: the same rectangle from logo_word_blocks, refilled from the pristine screen (cell + $0800, the copy at $8800) and the pristine colour data (cell + $0400, the copy at $8400 bound for $D800)

Run-length unpacker: read from ($07/$08) while it is below the end $0B/$0C, write to ($09/$0A). A count byte n below $80 is followed by n + 1 literal bytes; a count byte n of $80 or more is followed by one byte written n - $7F times (1 to 128). Used once, on file $01 (checked: the simulator's unpack of file $01 equals the title snapshot's picture)
Count byte: bit 7 clear = literal run, bit 7 set = repeat run
Literal run: copy n + 1 bytes (X = n down to 0)
Repeat run: write the byte, DEX, again while X is still $80 or more: n - $7F copies
Colour-RAM values for the 'ELECTRONIC ARTS' strip on row 0 (title_frame $40AE): $01 white, $07 yellow, indexed by bit 5 of the frame counter
Screen nibbles for the same strip ($40A8): $60 both times (multicolour %01 pixels blue, %10 black); only the colour RAM changes

Colours rolling down the three credit lines (title_frame $40C1): rows 19, 20, 21 take entries phase, phase + 1, phase + 2, phase 0-3, so six bytes are read: $01 white, $0F light grey, $0C grey, $0F, $01, $0F
One byte ($0C) between names_colours and ea_sweep_colours that no index reaches (names_colours reads up to $4368, ea_sweep_colours starts at $436A)

Colours for the EA logo's eight columns (title_frame $40DE): column c of phase p (0-7) takes entry p + c, so 15 bytes are read: grey $0C runs with light grey $0F and white $01 peaks, which move one column every two frames
One byte ($01) after ea_sweep_colours, past the highest index (14); not read

Screen nibbles (bitmap cell colours %01/%10) for the recoloured logo words, 242 bytes, row-major per word: SKATE at offset $00 (17 x 7 cells), OR at $77 (6 x 3), DIE! at $89 (15 x 7). logo_word_on copies them over the screen at $8000; the pristine values are in the copy at $8800
Colour-RAM nibbles (%11 pixel colour) for the same 242 cells, same offsets; logo_word_on writes them to $D800 + cell. With logo_word_screen they swap the logo's white face and brown shadow

Three rectangles of five bytes for logo_word_on/off: screen address lo/hi, width - 1, height - 1, offset into logo_word_screen/colour. 0 SKATE: $8050 (row 2, column 0), 17 x 7, offset $00; 1 OR: $80B2 (row 4, column 18), 6 x 3, offset $77; 2 DIE!: $8068 (row 2, column 24), 15 x 7, offset $89
Music: per-voice vibrato position (three bytes, voices 0-2), a triangle between 0 and vib_limit stepped once a frame by the effects code ($4790-$47AB)
Music: per-voice vibrato width, bits 3-6 of the instrument's vibrato byte ($4782)
Music: per-voice vibrato direction, bit 7 set while vib_counter is falling

MUSIC INIT (JMP $50DA): stops CIA 2 timer A, clears the filter routing ($D417 = 0), installs the sample NMI (vector $5106, CIA 2 timer A NMIs enabled) and asks music_play to reset every voice on its next call ($4B17 = $40). There is one tune: no tune number is taken, the voice tracks are fixed at $4C1B/$4C1E and the sample track at $4A18. Called by title_main at $401F

MUSIC STOP (JMP $50EB): $4B17 = $C0, so the next music_play stops the sample timer, clears the three voices' control registers and leaves the driver idle ($80). Called by title_main at $402D when fire is pressed

MUSIC PLAY, once a frame from the raster interrupt (title_frame $4093). Writes the volume $D418 = $0A (the sample NMI overwrites it between frames), then acts on the state $4B17: $40 (from music_init) resets each voice's track position, pattern index, duration counter and control byte, and the sample channel's track position, pattern index and duration, writes 0 to each voice's $D404 and $D406 and sets instrument 7 (the transpose is not reset), leaving $4B17 = 7 (the loop's last value, bits 6-7 clear: play); $C0 (music_stop) stops CIA 2 timer A, writes 0 to the three control registers and sets $80; $80 does nothing but the sample-channel check at $495D; anything else plays a frame: tempo ($45D4), the voice loop from voice 2 down to voice 0 ($45EF), then the sample channel ($495D)
State $40: reset the three voices (X = $4B15 = 2 down to 0)
State $C0: stop, or $80: idle

Tempo: a 5-frame counter $4B14 and a tick counter $4B12/$4B13 (reload 1). A tick (reading notes) happens when $4B14 is not 0 and $4B12 equals its reload; $4B12 is not stepped on the frame $4B14 wraps. The result, simulated: ticks 2 and 3 frames apart in turn, 2.5 frames a tick, 20 ticks a second on PAL. Between ticks only the effects run

Voice loop, X = voice 2 down to 0: $4AF3 = the voice's SID register offset (0, 7, 14). On a tick, voice 0 also counts down the sample channel's duration $4A14 ($4611); a voice whose duration counter $4AFA goes below zero reads its next note ($461F), the others go to the release check ($4744); between ticks every voice goes to the effects ($4758)

Read the voice's track (pointer from voice_track_lo/hi into $02/$03) at position $4AF4: a byte below $80 is a pattern number; $FF restarts the track at position 0 (and clears the pattern index and duration); $80-$FE sets the transpose $4B4D = byte & $7F and reads on

Read a note from the pattern (pointer from pattern_lo/hi into $04/$05) at index $4AF7. Command byte: bits 0-4 duration in ticks minus one ($4AFA); bit 6 a rest (no further bytes: gate off, AD/SR and control 0, $46B7); bit 7 an instrument byte follows ($4B06), or, if that byte has bit 7 set, two bytes stored at $4B21/$4B1E, which nothing but the vibrato's skip test reads ($47AE): a portamento that this driver never performs; bit 5 keeps the gate on to the end (no release on the last tick, $474A). Then the note byte: bits 0-6 plus the transpose index freq_table into $4B1B/$4B18; bit 7 ties the note (no new envelope or pulse, $46DB)
Rest: gate mask $FE, AD and SR = 0 on the voice, control 0

Note start: control byte from the instrument (instr_a + 2) into $4B0F; unless tied, the instrument's pulse width (instr_a + 0/1) goes to $D402/$D403 and to the pulse program's start ($4B28/$4B2B and $4B2E/$4B31), AD and SR (instr_a + 3/4) to $D405/$D406, the effect timer $4B3D from instr_b + 3, and the pulse program, its counter and the note's age $4B40 restart at 0. Then the control byte is stored, the pattern index steps on, and a following $FF ends the pattern (index 0, next track position); straight to the register write at $493C
Tick without a new note: on the last tick of the note (duration 0) the gate mask becomes $FE, so the release starts, unless the command byte had bit 5 set

Effects, every frame for a voice that did not start a note: Y = instrument * 8 ($4B16); fx flags (instr_a + 7) into $4B24, pulse program number (instr_a + 6) into $4B11, vibrato delay (instr_b + 5) patched into the CMP at $4800, vibrato byte (instr_a + 5): zero skips the vibrato
Vibrato: width = bits 3-6, shift = bits 0-2 of the vibrato byte; vib_counter moves one step a frame between 0 and the width, turning at each end. Skipped while a portamento byte is set ($4B21)

Vibrato pitch: step = freq_table[note] - freq_table[note - 1] with the note's age $4B40 added to its high byte, shifted right shift + 1 times (the high byte one more time than the low); frequency = freq_table[note] - step * (width / 2) + step * vib_counter, written to $4B1B/$4B18 only once the age has reached the instrument's delay ($4800). As written, the depth grows with the note's age (wrapping at 256 frames)
Operand of the CMP # at $4800: the vibrato delay in frames, patched every frame from instr_b + 5 at $4771 ($F0 in the snapshot, left by the last instrument read)

Pulse program (instr_a + 6 = 1 or 2; 0 = none): pointer from pulse_prog_lo/hi. When the voice's counter $4B37 runs out, read the next entry at $4B34: a byte below $80 = frames, then a signed step ($4B3A); $FE = stop (no more pulse writes); $FF = back to the start; $80-$FD = frames & $7F with the pulse width reset to the note's starting value, then a step. Each frame the step is added to the 16-bit width $4B28/$4B2B, written to $D402/$D403
Operand of the ADC # at $4887: $00 or $FF, patched at $487A from the sign of the pulse step so that the high byte of the width takes the step's sign extension

Drum program, when the instrument's fx bit 0 is set and the note is not a rest: pointer instr_b + 0/1 (instrument 2: drum_prog_a, instrument 6: drum_prog_b), index $4B49 (0 at each note). An entry below $80 is a control value for $4B00 and a 16-bit amount subtracted from the voice's frequency; $85 holds (registers written, index kept); any other byte of $80 or more goes straight to $D404 with the next byte straight to $D401 (frequency high), and the voice's stored registers are not written that frame

fx bit 6: while the effect timer lasts (decremented again here) the frequency is that of the note instr_b + 0 (a fixed attack pitch), then the note's own frequency is put back unless the instrument has a vibrato

SAMPLE PLAYER, the NMI of CIA 2 timer A (one per timer period, $91-$1C8 + 1 cycles: 2.2-6.8 kHz). A is saved into the operand at $514F. Each sample byte holds two 4-bit values, played high nibble first: the parity of $06 (incremented each NMI) picks the nibble, and the low-nibble NMI steps the pointer (the operand of LDA at $5110, patched by the sample event). The value goes to $D418, the SID's volume register: the 4-bit sample replaces the volume each time, which the chip turns into an audible level (the classic volume-register sample; filter-mode bits are left 0). A byte $1F is the end mark, tested before either nibble: with the loop flag set the pointer is reloaded from the loop address (operands at $511E/$5123), otherwise the timer is stopped. $DD0D is read to acknowledge, A restored, RTI. X and Y are not touched. Simulated: 176098 $D418 writes in 3000 frames of the title

TITLE ENTRY ($4000, file $00, jumped to by the boot). Blanks the screen (VIC $D011 bit 4 off), banks $01 = $25 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O in), then: load_title_picture (file $01, unpacked into the bitmap at $A000), show_title_picture (bitmap mode on, bank 2), load_samples (file $02 to $1000, the picture on screen meanwhile), install_title_irq (raster interrupt at line $FB, which plays the music and animates the colours), music_init. It then waits at $4022 for fire on either joystick port ($DC00 bit 4 for port 2, $DC01 bit 4 for port 1; SPACE also pulls $DC01 bit 4 while CIA 1 port A selects keyboard row 7, as the snapshot's $7F there does: simulated). On fire: music_stop and one more music_play call to silence the voices, the colour RAM and the screen are put back from the pristine copies at $8400 and $8800, wait_raster_wrap, the raster interrupt is turned off, file $03 (the shop) is loaded to $0880, $FDFF is cleared (the shop compares it with $55 at $0F6E/$0F83 of file $03 and, when it differs, loads file $0B, the event manager, to $C000), and the NMI vector is pointed at $0880 and CIA 2 timer A restarted ($DD0E = 1): the next timer underflow raises an NMI that enters the shop, while the CPU spins at $4090. The title never returns
$FDFF = 0: the shop ($0F83 in file $03) loads the event manager, file $0B, while it is not $55
